title: Aurora Clinic — Data Sovereignty, KMS & No-Train Affirmation
summary: Customer sought explicit contractual and technical assurances around prompt/content retention and a firm 'no training' commitment. Discussed BYOK/KMS options, audit log granularity, RBAC/SSO integration and regional isolation. Agreed to deliver SOC2 report copy, security architecture diagram, and contract language. Follow-up pilot to include brief benchmark and retention config demo.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08
Start: 15:00 UTC / 10:00 ET
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood Eng), Marta Ruiz (Aurora CISO), Dr Ethan Park (Aurora Head of AI), Samir Qureshi (Aurora Legal), Leah Chen (Aurora ProdOps)

--- Auto sections (generated) ---
Summary: short run-through of security controls and contractual 'no-train' language, plus KMS options
Action items: listed at end of transcript

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. quick roll call — alex here from redwood, priya and liam also on. Marta, Ethan, Samir — thanks for joining.
[00:20] Marta Ruiz: Hi all, thanks. we'll be pretty focused — main ask is we need hard assurances on data handling, especially prompts that contain PHI. we have regulatory workflows to keep to.
[00:33] Priya Nandakumar: totally understood. we'll walk through our SOC 2 posture, how we handle keys/KMS, and specifically how customer data is isolated and not used for training unless explicitly opted in.
[00:47] Dr. Ethan Park: quick context — we're evaluating an LLM assisted triage tool. latency is important but privacy and no-bleed of PHI into model weights is deal-critical.
[01:05] Liam Ortiz: to be explicit, by default Redwood's hosted endpoints do not use customer request data to further train public models. we can explain logging/retention too.
[01:20] Samir Qureshi: "do not use to further train" — we need that in contract language and proof of technical controls. not just a carrier phrase.
[01:34] Alex Mercer: absolutely. first, SOC 2: we are SOC 2 Type II for security and availability, report covers Nov 2025–Oct 2026. we can share the report under an NDA. link placeholder: https://redwood.internal/soc2-2026.pdf (we'll send official copy).
[01:58] Marta Ruiz: ok. what about ISO? any plans or certs?
[02:07] Priya Nandakumar: we don't have ISO 27001 cert yet, roadmap item for Q2 2027. SOC 2 is the primary cert we currently provide.
[02:20] Leah Chen: region/residency question — Aurora needs patient data kept in us-east and not replicated to eu. is that supported?
[02:32] Liam Ortiz: yes — region pinning is supported. for hosted we can pin tenancy/compute to us-east-1. for the strictest requirement we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated nodes run in the customer-specified region.
[02:50] Dr. Ethan Park: if we go hosted with region pinning, are backups or logs ever replicated across regions?
[03:02] Priya Nandakumar: backup copies are region-local by default; cross-region replication is only enabled for DR and must be configured per-customer. we can disable replication on request and document that in the runbook.
[03:20] Samir Qureshi: on KMS — we need BYOK and proof that keys can be rotated by us and that Redwood has no persistent access. how does that work?
[03:33] Liam Ortiz: we provide BYOK via Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and also HSM-backed options for Dedicated/Private. keys are used to encrypt model checkpoints and any at-rest storage. we do not persist plaintext keys; Redwood has an encrypted envelope, not the raw key. we can provide an architecture diagram.
[03:56] Marta Ruiz: can you show how the encryption boundary looks for prompts, logs, and cached KV? is the KV cache encrypted with the same key?
[04:12] Priya Nandakumar: KV cache and prefix-caches are encrypted at rest with customer key if BYOK is enabled; ephemeral in-memory caches are cleared per-session. logging levels are configurable — we can redact full prompt text from logs and only store metadata at chosen retention windows.
[04:34] Alex Mercer: note — there is a difference between telemetry logs and audit logs. audit logs are tamper-evident and include who/when/what for API calls, but we can redact content. telemetry might have aggregated token usage for billing.
[04:54] Dr. Ethan Park: what about prompt retention windows? we want prompts to be ephemeral by default — a maximum of 24 hours unless we opt in.
[05:06] Priya Nandakumar: default hosted retention is 30 days for debugging; but we support configuring shorter windows and ephemerality. for HIPAA workflows, we typically set ephemeral retention windows of 0–24 hours and disable long-term storage. that's configurable per-tenant and enforced by policy.
[05:26] Marta Ruiz: do ephemeral prompts still get into model monitoring or eval sets?
[05:33] Liam Ortiz: they do not get used to update model weights. monitoring can be done via hashed or redacted samples; any usage for model improvement requires explicit, auditable opt-in.
[05:46] Samir Qureshi: what is the evidence chain you can provide for "we did not train on customer data"?
[05:55] Priya Nandakumar: we provide three things: contractual no-training clause, an internal policy with change history (we can share excerpts), and operational proof points — retention settings, pipeline manifests showing opt-in toggles, and selective data flows in the architecture diagram. we also offer a signed attestation for enterprise.
[06:16] Marta Ruiz: ok — a signed attestation would be useful. we'll also ask for proof of the opt-in toggle being disabled by default in our tenant.
[06:27] Alex Mercer: we'll include a tenant config snapshot and the attestation.
[06:32] Leah Chen: audit-logs granularity — can we see prompt hashes, user id, API key id, model version, region and node id?
[06:45] Liam Ortiz: audit logs include timestamp, api key id, tenant id, model id and model version, request/response size, latency and a content-hash if enabled. content itself can be redacted or hashed. we can also include node identifier for debugging if you need it.
[06:59] Dr. Ethan Park: hashing prompts might still be reversible if salt reused — are salts per-tenant?
[07:08] Priya Nandakumar: yes salts are per-tenant and rotated. hashing algorithms follow current NIST recommendations. we'll provide cryptographic details in the security pack.
[07:23] Marta Ruiz: SSO and RBAC — we run Okta. do you support SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO?
[07:32] Alex Mercer: yes — we support SAML2.0 and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and role-based controls with custom roles for audit-only, dev, prod, etc.
[07:45] Samir Qureshi: need to ensure least privilege — can we map Okta groups to RBAC roles and have session timeout policies enforced?
[07:54] Liam Ortiz: yes, group-to-role mapping is supported; session durations and multi-factor enforcement can be required by policy.
[08:05] Leah Chen: logging retention — legal wants 7 years for some audit trails, is that possible?
[08:12] Priya Nandakumar: we can retain audit logs for long-term storage to a customer-owned bucket (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) or to a managed archive and we can sign retention agreements. long retention is typically exportable to your long-term archive.
[08:27] Dr. Ethan Park: about PHI — do you offer any additional processing mode, like redaction-in-flight or PII scrubbers before logs or persistence?
[08:38] Priya Nandakumar: yes — there is a pre-persist pipeline where customers can install content filters or use Redwood's PII scrubber. redaction can be applied to logs or replaced with token markers. We also support a middleware hook so customers can run their PII filter in their VPC before sending to Redwood Private.
[08:58] Marta Ruiz: Great. one more angle on the "no training" claim — if Redwood itself trains models (e.g., open research) using publicly scraped corpora, how do you guarantee no inadvertent bleed from tenant-kept caches?
[09:12] Liam Ortiz: there's a clear boundary — tenant data does not flow into our internal training pipelines. archives marked as customer-owned are inaccessible to internal training clusters. Any dataset used for research is from public or explicitly opt-in corpora. internal monitoring ensures that tenant buckets are excluded via automations.
[09:32] Samir Qureshi: can we get a signed attestation plus a technical runbook showing the automation that enforces exclusion?
[09:40] Alex Mercer: yes, we can provide both.
[09:44] Marta Ruiz: on legal terms — we'd like a clause that says "Redwood shall not use Customer Content to improve or train any models without Customer's prior written consent" and a right to audit.
[09:58] Samir Qureshi: also need defined breach notification timelines and forensics support SLA.
[10:07] Alex Mercer: standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents; for enterprise we can negotiate tighter windows and forensic support commitments.
[10:17] Leah Chen: curious: if we run in Redwood Private in our VPC, do you still need to have any control plane access?
[10:26] Priya Nandakumar: Private has two modes — fully air-gapped where Redwood only ships the software and no control-plane access, or hybrid where control plane calls home for metrics; in hybrid mode metrics can be disabled. For strict regulatory needs, air-gapped with on-prem support is available.
[10:46] Dr. Ethan Park: latency tradeoff — I assume Private increases management overhead and might affect autoscaling — any guidance?
[10:53] Liam Ortiz: Dedicated provides predictable throughput with less ops overhead; Private gives you full control but you take on infra ops. we have an onboarding runbook and SRE support packages if you pick Private.
[11:07] Marta Ruiz: small follow — when you say "no training" by default for hosted: is there ever a case where Redwood's defaults change? we need a contractual lock.
[11:18] Alex Mercer: defaults are codified in the service terms; any change would be notice and opt-in for existing customers. we'll include fixed contractual language and the attestation.
[11:30] Samir Qureshi: for audit logs, can we get a regular feed into our SIEM? Splunk/Datadog?
[11:38] Liam Ortiz: yes streams to Splunk/Datadog/Kafka or to your S3 bucket. we can set up an event-forwarding pipeline and ensure it's encrypted in transit with mTLS.
[11:50] Dr. Ethan Park: question about model variants — if you do fallback to smaller models, is there any difference in logging or retention?
[11:58] Priya Nandakumar: behavior is consistent across model variants; logs and retention policies are tenant-level and apply irrespective of model used. model variant only affects compute and latency, not retention.
[12:12] Marta Ruiz: got it. do you have a hardened process for privileged access reviews?
[12:18] Alex Mercer: yes — we do quarterly privileged access reviews and ephemeral privileged sessions for SRE with just-in-time elevation, all recorded in audit logs.
[12:30] Leah Chen: curious about incident forensics — will you hand over relevant logs if there's a suspected exfil?
[12:36] Liam Ortiz: yes, subject to legal and confidentiality obligations, we'll provide necessary logs and cooperate with forensics. we also support live packet capture in Private for deep diagnostics if required.
[12:52] Samir Qureshi: edge case — if a customer accidentally includes PHI in a prompt and it appears in a debug log snapshot retained for 30 days, what's the remediation?
[13:03] Priya Nandakumar: remediation steps: immediate redaction/expunge from logs, rotation of any exposed keys, notify customer, and optional locking of the tenant to prevent further writes while we investigate. we can provide playbooks.
[13:18] Marta Ruiz: we'll want defined SLAs for remediation times.
[13:24] Alex Mercer: we'll propose SLAs in follow-up.
[13:28] Dr. Ethan Park: for our proof-of-concept, we want to run a small dataset and see the retention settings in action and verify logs go to our SIEM. can that be done in two weeks?
[13:39] Liam Ortiz: two weeks is reasonable for a scoped POC with dedicated support, yes.
[13:45] Leah Chen: any blockers for that POC from your side?
[13:49] Priya Nandakumar: just the paperwork and access to your SIEM endpoints and a sample tenant. we'll need an NDA and a quick infra checklist.
[13:58] Samir Qureshi: paperwork timeline — Legal here can turn around the DPA and the no-training addendum in about five business days if your legal team is responsive.
[14:09] Alex Mercer: our legal is ready; we'll circulate the addendum and DPA language for your review.
[14:18] Marta Ruiz: great. any competitors we should be mindful of? we evaluated Anthropic and had concerns about their training opt-out clarity.
[14:29] Priya Nandakumar: noted. we find customers compare us on observability and contractual clarity.
[14:35] Dr. Ethan Park: final quick question — can you provide a cryptographic proof-of-possession or attestation that customer keys are not exported?
[14:45] Liam Ortiz: we can provide KMS key usage logs and a key access policy dump, plus HSM attestations where available. for some clouds we can share CloudHSM attestation docs.
[14:59] Alex Mercer: ok, next steps summary — we'll send SOC 2 under NDA, the security architecture diagram, tenant config snapshot showing retention toggles, signed no-train attestation, and sample DPA language. we'll also propose a 2-week POC kickoff slot.
[15:22] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. would like the DPA to list 0–24 hour default retention for prompts for the POC.
[15:31] Samir Qureshi: and we'll review addendum; please include breach notification SLA and forensic support clause.
[15:39] Leah Chen: can you schedule the POC kickoff for week of Nov 23? that's our availability.
[15:46] Alex Mercer: yes we'll propose times. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
[15:53] Dr. Ethan Park: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[15:58] Marta Ruiz: appreciate it.
[16:03] Alex Mercer: bye all.

--- End transcript ---
